findings.title: Shard-split queries have template variables and ad-hoc filters applied twice
findings.body: This interpolates targets with `applyTemplateVariables` before shard discovery, then every generated shard request is passed to `runSplitQuery`, which now calls `applyTemplateVariables` again on those already-interpolated targets. When `request.filters` contains ad-hoc filters, the filter matchers are injected both times; this can produce duplicate/conflicting label matchers or otherwise change the query sent to Loki. The previous path interpolated once. Preserve the initial interpolation needed for shard discovery, but avoid applying filters/template processing a second time when delegating the already-prepared shard request to `runSplitQuery`.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to an empty expression are not discarded
findings.body: The code filters empty expressions before calling `applyTemplateVariables`, so a target such as `{ expr: "$query" }` whose variable resolves to an empty string remains in the splitting groups. It is then classified and sent as an empty LogQL expression instead of receiving the existing empty-query behavior (ignore it). Filter again after interpolation, or interpolate before the empty-expression filter, so an empty variable value does not result in a backend parse/error request.

findings.title: An expression emptied by interpolation can leave the shard path with no runnable requests
findings.body: As in the time-splitting path, emptiness is tested before interpolation. If interpolation turns the expression into an empty string, this target is retained in the shard group and later passed to `runSplitQuery`. `runSplitQuery` then filters that empty target out before building requests, leaving an empty request list; its grouped runner attempts to start from `requests[0]` and can fail rather than cleanly ignoring the query. Perform the empty-expression filtering after `applyTemplateVariables` in this entry point.
